title: Poulet au Cidre
subtitle: Normandy chicken braised in dry cider with creme fraiche
excerpt: Bone-in chicken pieces braised in dry cider with shallots and thyme, then finished with creme fraiche for a rich, slightly tart sauce. A classic from the apple orchards of Normandy.
sourceNotes: Norman recipe using the region's famous cider; chicken in cider with cream is one of the most recognised dishes from Normandy.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the creme fraiche. Reheat gently and stir in fresh creme fraiche when serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales well for a larger crowd. Use a wide casserole so the chicken sits in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead without the creme fraiche. Reheat and finish with cream just before serving.

content.text: Poulet au cidre is a one-pot Norman braise with a rich, apple-scented sauce. Use a dry cider rather than a sweet one so the sauce does not cloy. Brown the chicken well before braising; that colour builds the flavour.
Pat the chicken dry with kitchen paper. Season all over with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil and butter in a wide casserole over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches, skin side down first, for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the shallots to the pan, cut side down. Cook for 3 minutes until lightly coloured. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cider and bring to a simmer, scraping up any brown bits from the base. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return the chicken to the pan, skin side up. The liquid should come about halfway up the pieces. Cover and simmer on a low heat for 30 minutes.
Remove the lid. Increase the heat slightly and cook for 10 more minutes to reduce the liquid a little and crisp the skin.
Stir in the creme fraiche and mustard if using. Simmer for 3 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning. Discard the bay leaves and thyme before serving.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and pale.
items.cause: The chicken was not browned well enough, or the cider did not reduce.
items.fix: Remove the chicken, increase the heat, and reduce the sauce to a coating consistency before stirring in the creme fraiche.

items.symptom: The creme fraiche has split into greasy pools.
items.cause: The heat was too high when it was added.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low when adding cream. Stir constantly and do not let it return to a full boil.

items.cause: The cider was very dry and the liquid did not reduce enough.
items.fix: Reduce the sauce further before adding cream. The creme fraiche will mellow it, but the base needs to cook down first.
